rows.text: Resolves the stack index `edx` against the state at `rcx` to a 16-byte value slot: a positive index is taken from the current frame's base (the first qword of the record at `rcx+0x20`) and replaced by `01CCB510` when not below the top at `rcx+0x10` (unsigned); an index above -1001000 is taken from the top; exactly -1001000 gives the slot at `+0x40` of the object at `rcx+0x18`; lower indexes select upvalue number -1001000 minus the index of the frame's function closure (slot (n+1)*0x10), or `01CCB510` when the function value's type dword is 0x16 or the number exceeds the closure's byte `+0xA` (signed); it then calls `0081F580` with the slot's qword and `r8d`, copies the returned 16-byte value (qword plus type dword `+8`) to the top and advances the top by 0x10.

Measures the pattern string at `r8`, sets up a stack buffer record (inline 0x200-byte area, length 0, owner `rcx`) and repeatedly finds the pattern in the subject `rdx` with the import at `008C2A08`; for each hit it appends the subject bytes before the hit and then the whole replacement string `r9`, each append first growing the buffer when the free space is too small (new size doubled, or length plus need, calling `00812960` with `01CCA278` on overflow, allocating through `00810240`, copying with `00861EBA` and calling `00810D20` with -2 when the old storage was not the inline area) before copying with `00861EBA`, and resumes after the pattern; when no hit remains it appends the rest of the subject through `00813450` and `00861EBA`, pushes the buffered bytes with `008105C0`, calls `00810D20` with -2 when the storage is not inline, and returns the result of `00811530` with -1 and 0, checking the stack cookie through `00808C40`.

Calls `00812890` with `xmm1` = 502.0 (`01CCA3C4`) and `0080F420` with `r8d` + 0x14, raising through `00812960` with `01CCA240` and `01CCA308` when that returns zero; then, for each 16-byte entry of the array at `rdx` until one whose first qword is null, it calls `00810730` with minus `r8d` repeated `r8d` times (skipped when `r8d` is not positive), `00810470` with the entry's second qword and `r8d`, and `00810DF0` with -2 minus `r8d` and the entry's first qword; finally it tail-jumps to `00811130` with the bitwise NOT of `r8d`.

With the frame record at `rcx+0x20`: when byte `rcx+0x48` has bit `0x2` or `0x4` set it first, for bit `0x2` only, calls `0081DA20` with 1 and -1 (keeping the `rdx` source position relative to the stack base `rcx+0x38`), then copies the previous frame's (`+0x10`) qword `+0x38` to `rcx+0x28`; it makes the previous frame current at `rcx+0x20`, copies 16-byte values from `rdx` to the frame's function slot (`[frame]`) onward while the signed word count at frame `+0x20` is not exhausted and the source is below the top `rcx+0x10` (unsigned), sets the type dword of the remaining wanted slots to 0 while the count stays positive, stores the end position to `rcx+0x10`, and returns the word count plus 1.

Using the state at `rcx+0x38`, calls `0081EFB0` with it and the incoming `rdx` and `r8`, pushes the returned object on that state's stack (qword plus a type dword equal to the object's byte `+8` OR 0x40) and calls `0081FB80` with the qword at `+8` of the record at `rcx+0x30` and the pushed slot; when the returned slot's type dword is 0 it writes 1 to its value and type dwords and, if the qword at `+0x18` of the state's `+0x18` record is greater than zero (signed), calls `0081A8A0`; it then pops the slot (top minus 0x10) and returns the `0081EFB0` result.

With block record B at `rcx+0x20` and lexer L at `rcx+0x18`: if B has a predecessor (qword `+0`) and byte `+0xD` set it calls `0082FB30`, then `0082FD80` with that result and B's byte `+0xC`, then `0082FE20` with it; if B's byte `+0xE` is set it interns `01CCBCEC` with `0081EF90`, adds a label with `0082C310` (list at `+0x20` of L's `+0x50` record, dword `+0x28` of L's `+0x30` record) and passes that 0x18-byte entry to `0082A7C0`; it then makes the predecessor current, adds B's byte `+0xC` minus byte `rcx+0x42` to dword `+8` of the `+0x50` record, and while `rcx+0x42` exceeds B's `+0xC` decrements it and stores dword `rcx+0x28` into field `+0xC` of the 16-byte entry in the array at `[[rcx]+0x30]` numbered by the signed word at index `+0x42` + dword `rcx+0x3C` of the word array at `[[L+0x50]]`, copies `+0x42` to `+0x44` and B's signed word `+8` to dword `+0x28` of the `+0x50` record; with a predecessor it calls `0082C0B0` and returns, it returns when B's signed word `+0xA` is not below the record's dword `+0x18`, else it formats `01CCD0C0` (name byte `+8` = 4 and byte `+0xA` above 0) or `01CCD0E8` via `0081BFF0`, clears L's dword `+0x10` and calls `00824330`, where the range ends.

When the token dword `rcx+0x10` is not 0x120 it gets the token text from `00824340` with 0x120, formats `01CCCFC8` with it through `0081BFF0` and calls `00824330`, where the range ends; otherwise it saves the qword `rcx+0x18`, calls `00824260`, calls `0082C220` with the saved qword, increments byte `+0x42` of the function record at `rcx+0x30` and writes that record's dword `+0x28` into field `+8` of the 16-byte entry (array at qword `+0x30` of the record's first qword) numbered by the signed word at position dword `+0x3C` plus the new count minus 1 of the word array at the first qword of the `+0x50` record of the record's `+0x18` object, calls `00829B10` with a stack record, 0 and dword `rcx+4`, then writes dword `+0x28` again into field `+8` of the entry numbered the same way from dword `+0x3C` plus the stack record's dword `+4`, and returns after the stack-cookie check through `00808C40`.

Saves byte `+0x44` of the function record at `rcx+0x30`; when the token dword `rcx+0x10` is 0x120 it raises a limit error if the dword at `rdx+0x18` is above 2147483645 (signed), formatting `01CCD000` with `01CCD128`, that limit and either `01CCCFD8` or `0081BFF0` of `01CCCFE8` with dword `+0x68` of the record's first-qword object and calling `00824330`; otherwise it saves `rcx+0x18`, calls `00824260` and makes a stack key record of kind 4 holding the `00830510` result for the saved qword; for any other token it calls `00824260`, parses the key with `0082D470` and `0082F8E0`, and requires token 0x5D (else `00824340`, `0081BFF0` with `01CCCFC8` and `00824330`) before calling `00824260`; it then increments the dword at `rdx+0x18`, requires token 0x3D the same way, calls `00824260`, converts the key with `0082F660`, parses the value with `0082D470` and converts it with `0082F660`, emits through `0082F450` with 0xA, the dword at `+4` of the record at `rdx+0x10` and both results, restores byte `+0x44` and returns after the stack-cookie check through `00808C40`; the listing stops inside the 0x3D error path.

With the function record at `rcx+0x30`: when the token dword `rcx+0x10` minus 0x104 is at most 0x1A (unsigned) and its bit is set in mask 0x4020007, or the token is 0x3B, it passes first 0 and count 0; otherwise it parses an expression into a stack record with `0082D470` and, while the token is 0x2C, calls `00824260`, `0082F860` and `0082D470` again, counting expressions; when the record's kind dword is 12 or 13 it calls `00830350` with -1 and, for kind 12 with a single expression, rewrites the code dword the record indexes (array at `+0x18` of the function record's first qword) by clearing bits `0x21` and setting `0x1E`, passing byte `+0x42` as first and -1 as count; for other kinds one expression passes the `0082F780` result as first and several pass byte `+0x42` after `0082F860`, with the expression count; it then calls `00830120` with first and count, calls `00824260` when the token is 0x3B, and returns after the stack-cookie check through `00808C40`.

Works on the instruction indexed by dword `rdx+4` in the code array at `+0x18` of the record `[rcx]`: when the kind dword `[rdx]` is 12 it replaces the instruction's `0x7FC000` field with `r8d` + 1 and returns; when it is 13 it replaces the field above `0x7FFFFF` with `r8d` + 1 and the `0x3FC0` field with byte `rcx+0x44`, and when that byte plus 1 exceeds byte `+0x7A` of the record `[rcx]` (signed) it either calls `00824330` with `01CCD330` (when the sum is at least 0xFA) or stores the sum to `+0x7A`, then increments byte `+0x44`; other kinds return unchanged.

Returns at once when `edx` is -1; otherwise walks the jump chain through the code array at `+0x18` of the record `[rcx]`: for each index it derives the next one from the instruction's field above `0x3FFF` (field minus 0x1FFFF, with -1 ending the chain), takes the preceding instruction as the control when the index is at least 1 and the byte table at `01CCCCD0` has a negative entry for that instruction's opcode (`0x3F` field), and when the control's opcode is 0x1C either sets its `0x3FC0` field to `r9d` (when `r9d` is neither 0xFF nor equal to the control's field above `0x7FFFFF`) or rewrites it to opcode 0x1B with that top field moved into `0x3FC0` and the `0x7FC000` field kept, then points the jump at `r8d`; for other control opcodes it points the jump at the fifth argument; the jump field is set to target minus index minus 1 plus 0x1FFFF, and a distance whose absolute value exceeds 0x1FFFF (signed `jg`) calls `00824330` with `01CCD308`, where the range ends.

corrections.why: byte re-read by a non-drafting agent: 'the 16-byte variable entry it indexes' is not what the bytes do: the entry index is the signed word at position byte `+0x42` plus dword `rcx+0x3C` of the word array that is the first qword of the lexer's `+0x50` record (`0082BA73`..`0082BA88`), and the 16-byte entries are in the array at qword `+0x30` of `[rcx]` (`0082BA8D`..`0082BA9A`).

byte re-read by a non-drafting agent: 'the 16-byte variable entry selected by the new count minus 1' / 'selected by the stack record's dword `+4`' hide an indirection: the position is dword `+0x3C` of the function record plus that value, it indexes a signed-word array (first qword of the `+0x50` record of the function record's `+0x18` object), and that word numbers the 16-byte entry in the array at qword `+0x30` of the function record's first qword (`0082BB8E`..`0082BBC1`, `0082BBD5`..`0082BC01`).

byte re-read by a non-drafting agent: 'the record's line dword' is not on the function record: it is dword `+0x68` of the function record's first-qword object (`0082C72A mov rax, qword ptr [rsi]`, `0082C72D mov r8d, dword ptr [rax + 0x68]`).
